{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABiJJPTA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhLg5BY", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 235, "title": "Remove bundled demos and redundant media insertion UI; capture the mouse with Pointer Lock on click", "body": "## Maintainer scope clarification — finish the existing PR #236

**Updated 2026-11-25: prioritize completing this Issue now.** This clarification supersedes the earlier detailed mouse edge-case requirements and acceptance criteria. It applies to this Issue and PR #236 only; it does not change the repository-wide review policy.

PR #236 already implements the requested UI simplification and Pointer Lock, with substantial implementation and validation work. At the time of this clarification, its head `9a3d6b0b7f7e4d3ed58e6bd30937fee7422bdbff` has passed [Emulator acceptance](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/actions/runs/45552472197), and GitHub reports a clean, mergeable PR.

**Use the current implementation as the completion candidate. Do not restart, redesign, or continue polishing it merely to address increasingly narrow hypothetical edge cases.** Perform a final, bounded review against the mandatory criteria below, reuse valid existing test evidence, and approve/merge/close #235 promptly if no actual blocking defect remains. Follow existing required branch protections. This is not authorization to ignore a known serious defect or a failing required check.

## Goal

Follow up on #233 by permanently removing the two bundled demo programs and their launcher, removing the redundant automatic-insertion button, and replacing the opt-in mouse checkbox with automatic click-to-capture Pointer Lock. The primary goal is a simpler player that works naturally for ordinary desktop PC-98 gameplay.

The removed features need no backward compatibility, deprecated aliases, dormant code, feature flags, or provisions for restoring them. Remove their active implementation and assets completely from the current repository and distribution; do not rewrite published Git history or historical Issue/PR records.

## 1. Remove both bundled demo programs completely

- Remove Star Trail and Hello world + BEEP, the Demos button/picker, exclusively demo-related source, binaries/disk images, handlers, UI state, CSS, build/publication paths, tests, and current help/documentation/license notices specific to those removed assets.
- Preserve required license notices for remaining content, the bundled FreeDOS HDD, generic disk boot/import, and independently useful test-only fixtures. Migrate substantive regressions formerly using demos to original test-only or existing legally usable non-demo fixtures. No need to preserve obsolete demo-specific behavior or tests.

## 2. Remove the redundant Insert media button

- Remove the standalone `#drive-auto` automatic-insertion button, its exclusive picker entry path/state, and unused styles or references. No replacement general-purpose insert button or compatibility alias.
- Keep each IDE HDD/FDD1/FDD2 Insert/Change picker, scoped Choose local file/Eject/Export actions, and screen/slot drag-and-drop. Screen drops retain automatic format routing; slot drops target the specific drive.
- Keep existing media format validation, dirty-HDD safeguards, export/recovery, Restore FreeDOS, separate boot selection, local-only media, and current disk I/O behavior. Cancel must not discard a mounted disk, and floppy insertion must not reset the guest.

## 3. Basic Pointer Lock behavior

- Remove the mouse-enable checkbox and its exclusive state/handlers. No manual enable step.
- Clicking the running PC-9821Ap guest canvas (raw or CRT) requests Pointer Lock from the user gesture, hides the host cursor, and captures input. The acquisition click itself must not activate the guest.
- Ordinary relative motion and left/right press/release must work, including motion beyond the canvas edge. Escape releases capture and restores host cursor/control access; a new deliberate click can recapture. Preserve normal keyboard input and the F12 escape-to-controls convention. Do not capture automatically on startup or in VM.
- Leaving the guest, pausing, resetting or changing machines must not leave the user trapped, the host cursor hidden indefinitely, or input stuck in ordinary use. If Pointer Lock is unsupported or denied, recover safely; retain existing simple bounded fallback where already implemented. Touch users should retain basic access to the player.
- Minimal Help text explains click-to-capture, Esc-to-release and relevant guest driver limitations.

## Mandatory pre-merge acceptance (revised and complete)

1. Both demo programs and the Demos launcher are removed from the current tree/build/publication; obsolete demo-only paths are removed and independent regression coverage is retained.
2. The standalone Insert media button is removed. Existing per-drive media operations and normal FreeDOS boot remain usable, including drag/drop, export and data-loss safeguards.
3. Native Pointer Lock works in a supported desktop browser for the basic flow: capture-only initial click, relative mouse movement, ordinary left/right clicks and release, Escape unlock, and deliberate recapture. No checkbox is required. No ordinary-use stuck input, capture trap or failure to recover host controls.
4. There is no demonstrated serious regression in normal keyboard/mouse operation, media safety, boot/reset, CRT display, audio continuity or emulator performance caused by this PR. Existing applicable mandatory checks and repository branch protections still pass.
5. Reuse the already recorded native/Wasm/browser/publication/audio validation and successful acceptance CI for the unchanged reviewed candidate. If a genuinely blocking change is necessary, run appropriate focused tests and applicable final required CI for the revised head. Do not rerun identical successful full suites or manufacture additional gates just because another review cycle occurred.

## Explicitly nonblocking / deferred scope

The following are no longer required for this Issue to close, **unless there is concrete evidence of a serious defect affecting the mandatory ordinary-use workflow above**:

- Exhaustive combinations of delayed Pointer Lock grants/errors, overlapping retries, cancellation races, unusual browser/OS-specific capture timing, and rare fallback re-entry or touch gestures.
- Perfect fidelity for every Ap mouse latch/nibble read sequence, unusually delayed guest polling, complex drag transitions, rapid mixed-button sequences, queue saturation, and other specialized bus-mouse timing scenarios.
- Further broadening of mouse hardware emulation, queue policy, browser compatibility matrices, test permutations, refactors, documentation polishing or speculative correctness/performance work unrelated to a mandatory criterion.

Already implemented and validated improvements may remain; do not revert or rewrite them simply because they are no longer mandatory. Record any concrete, nonblocking unresolved defects as follow-up candidates (or link an existing Issue); do not require implementing them, creating speculative Issues, or exhaustively searching for more before merging this PR.

## Final review / completion instruction (this Issue only)

The implementer and reviewer should evaluate the current PR #236 as a finished candidate, not begin another open-ended discovery cycle. A request for changes must identify a **specific reproducible or otherwise demonstrably serious defect** tied to one of the revised mandatory criteria, or a genuine required-check/protection failure. Minor or hypothetical findings are nonblocking; record them separately and stop expanding the current work.

If any actual blocker remains, list it concisely with evidence and the smallest necessary fix; resolve it without introducing unrelated requirements. Otherwise, approve and merge the existing PR and close #235 using the normal workflow. Do not withhold completion solely for optional validation, additional polish, or the possibility of future improvements.

## Required post-merge verification

None beyond the standard publication lifecycle.
